newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut judge wants 78 alleged pro-Israelis jailed.
newsitem.headline: Beirut judge wants 78 alleged pro-Israelis jailed.

text.p: A Lebanese military investigating judge demanded on Thursday up to 10 years imprisonment for 78 Lebanese men for allegedly collaborating with Israel, judicial sources said.
Lebanon and Israel are officially in a state of war and Lebanese laws forbid citizens from contacting or dealing with the Jewish state.
The sources said magistrate Riyad Taly demanded the imprisonment in absentia for all the suspects -- residents of Israel's 15-km (nine miles)-wide south Lebanon occupation zone.
Taly named in his indictment Akl Hashem, a high rank officer in Israel's local militia, the South Lebanon army (SLA).
Lebanon's military court had sentenced to death in absentia last December the head of the SLA, General Antoine Lahd, on the same charges.
Under Lebanese law, people sentenced in absentia are retried when they surrender or get arrested.
